hints.content:
The basic function $\sin(x)$ intersects its midline at $(0,0)$ and has a maximum point at $\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2},1\right)$.

$\qquad$![](${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/a341a449700483900a5e0b9fc1fc0ab4.png)

Let's transform $\pink{\sin(x)}$ to $\blue{0.5\sin(0.25x+0.75\pi)-5}$ step by step and see how the graph changes along the way.

The transformation from $\pink{\sin(x)}$ to $\green{\sin(0.25x)}$ is a horizontal stretch by a factor of $\dfrac{1}{0.25}=4$, so the maximum point's horizontal distance from the origin is stretched from $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ to $2\pi$.

$\qquad$[[☃ image 1]]

The transformation from $\green{\sin(0.25x)}$ to $\red{0.5\sin(0.25x)}$ is a vertical shrink by a factor of $2$, so the maximum point's vertical distance from the origin is shrunk from $1$ to $0.5$.

$\qquad$[[☃ image 2]]

options.alt: A dashed graph and a solid graph trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by pi and the y axis scales by one. On the dashed graph there is a point on the graph at the midline at (zero, zero) and a point at the maximum next to the mentioned point at (pi over two, one). On the solid graph, there is a point on the graph at the midline at (zero, zero) and a point at the maximum next to the mentioned point around (two pi, one).

A dashed graph and a solid graph trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by pi and the y axis scales by one. On the dashed graph there is a point on the graph at the midline at (zero, zero) and a point at the maximum next to the mentioned point at (two pi, one). On the solid graph, there is a point on the graph at the midline at (zero, zero) and a point at the maximum next to the mentioned point around (two pi, one half).

hints.content: The transformation from $\red{0.5\sin(0.25x)}$ to $\blue{0.5\sin(0.25x+0.75\pi)-5}$, which is equivalent to $0.5\sin{\large(}0.25(x+3\pi){\large)}-5$, is a translation to the left by $3\pi$ units and a translation downwards by $5$ units.

As a result of these transformations, the intersection point with the midline is now at $\left(-3\pi,-5\right)$ and the maximum point is at $(-\pi,-4.5)$.

The resulting graph looks as follows:

$\qquad$[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A  graph of a trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by pi and the y axis scales by one. On the graph, there is a point on the graph at the midline at (negative three pi, negative five) and a point at the maximum next to the mentioned point around (negative pi, negative four and one half).
